method: Five authored fictional questions, one live call per case; development checks, not held-out or repeated variation evaluation

observed.text: Stress can be a mental or physical response to an outside demand, such as schoolwork. This is general information from NIMH, not an assessment of your experience. This prototype does not determine a cause, diagnose a condition or choose treatment.

cases.question: Can it remember my usual cue?

observed.text: Choose a cue, then select Remember this choice if you want it restored next time. Reset preference removes it. Use this cue next time in History only copies the setting for review; it does not remember it or start an exercise. Changes during practice apply to that session.

cases.question: Does this app infer stress from clicks?

observed.text: No questionnaire or mood check-in is required. You can start directly, choose your cue, or ask an optional question. The app does not infer stress or a diagnosis from clicks, question wording or session history. Personalization uses an explicit cue choice that you can reset.

I am an educational assistant for this fictional coursework prototype, not a therapist. I can explain reviewed app content and general stress information. I cannot diagnose, provide treatment, or monitor anyone. Use fictional questions only.

The reading links distinguish general information from professional references and book listings. NIMH provides a public stress fact sheet; AIS lists military/veteran resources; Grey House describes a handbook whose full text has not been supplied; APA explains the DSM. These links do not turn this prototype into therapy or a diagnostic tool.
